title: Sheinbaum: US Decision to Name Cartels ‘Terrorists’ ‘Must Not Be a Pretext for an Invasion’
author: Emir Olivares
content:
_This article by[Emir
Olivares](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Emir%20Olivares,%20enviado)
originally appeared in the [September 4, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/04/politica/no-es-gasto-
es-inversion-sheinbaum-defiende-programas-de-bienestar), Mexico's premier
left-wing daily newspaper._

Aguascalientes, Ags. In her first accountability report in a state governed by
the opposition, two years into her administration, President Claudia Sheinbaum
Pardo stressed, as part of the country's **" profound changes,"** that the
United States' decision to designate organized crime as terrorist groups **"
must not be a pretext for an invasion,"** and **" that is how we put it in
Article 40 of the Constitution,"** she said.

She recalled that she also sent an initiative to the Congress of the Union to
bar people with dual nationality from being candidates for the Presidency of
the Republic, for governor, or for the head of government of Mexico City. **"
They must be exclusively Mexican."**

The president also defended the welfare programs, noting that **" there are
some who don't like them, because they say too much money is spent,"** but
that when people are supported, **" the one who has the least, the economy
flourishes,"** she said.

> It is not spending, it is investment.
>
> Claudia Sheinbaum

She stated that **" it is not spending, it is investment, because when senior
citizens have support, we are investing in Mexican families so that they can
have the minimum, the basics to get ahead."**

When we give a scholarship to students, **" it is not spending, it is
investment in education for young people, for the children of Mexico; when we
invest in a school, it is not spending, it is investment so that education can
be had; and when we invest in support for the countryside, for farmers, it is
not spending, it is investment so that the land can be cultivated; and so with
each one of the welfare programs."**

She emphasized that this year one trillion pesos is allocated to the programs.
**" It is a vision of solidarity, of fraternity; that is why the programs
today are social rights."**

During the assembly, attendees voiced rejection of the PAN governor, Teresa
Jiménez, throughout her welcome speech, despite a call for respect from the
head of the Federal Executive.

Thus, in the San Marcos neighborhood, in the state capital, Teresa Jiménez, of
the PAN, welcomed her amid jeers.

She put to a vote of the attendees whether to allow the opposition governor to
speak. The majority approved it. **" Practically unanimously, we are going to
respect one another,"** Sheinbaum said. But even so, the rejection continued
until the PAN representative stopped speaking.

**" Aguascalientes receives you with respect and hospitality. Your visit
represents an opportunity to strengthen the dialogue between the federation
and the states and to renew our shared responsibility,"** Jiménez told her,
and affirmed that Aguascalientes **" will rise to the occasion and do its
part."**

And she expanded on the social supports. Supporting those who have the least
**" is a vision of solidarity, of fraternity. That is why the welfare programs
today are constitutional rights."**

She cited that in Aguascalientes 420,952 people are supported directly,
without intermediaries, she stressed. **" It is an investment of nine billion
pesos."**

Among the supports, she mentioned that 137,717 senior citizens aged 65 and
over receive their bimonthly pension of 6,400 pesos **" and each year the
pension will increase above inflation."**

She also mentioned that 19,000 people with disabilities receive a pension;
474,402 high school students are on scholarships, and all girls and boys in
public schools receive support.
